title: Residential Improvement Guidelines and Residential Site Restrictions
meta: Revised July 12, 2024 · prepared by the Architectural Review Committee

blocks.x: These Residential Improvement Design Guidelines and Architectural Standards are intended to assist homeowners in Fossil Lake in the design of their homes and landscaping and other improvements to their property, and as provided for in Article IX, Sections 4 and 5 of the Declaration of Covenants, to list the rules and regulations adopted by the Homeowners Association with respect to the use of Residential Sites.
THE DECLARATION OF COVENANTS FOR FOSSIL LAKE P.U.D. REQUIRES PRIOR APPROVAL OF THE ARCHITECTURAL REVIEW COMMITTEE BEFORE ANY IMPROVEMENT TO PROPERTY INVOLVING A RESIDENTIAL LOT IN FOSSIL LAKE RANCH.

“Improvement to property” is very broadly defined in the Covenants. For instance, an “improvement to property” would include any landscaping or change of the grade of property; the construction or installation of any accessory building, patio, deck, pool or hot tub; the demolition or removal of any building or other improvement; and any change of exterior appearance of a building or other improvement. In order to assist homeowners, the Covenants authorize the Architectural Review Committee (hereinafter “ARC”) to establish guidelines and to establish certain pre-approved designs for several types of improvements to property and to exempt certain improvements to property from the requirement for approval. This booklet contains the guidelines established by the Architectural Review Committee with respect to residential property. Throughout this document the term “property” shall refer to a residential site.
In addition to the introductory material, these Guidelines contain:
a listing of specific types of improvements which homeowners might wish to make with specific Information as to each of these types of improvements;
Rules and regulations applicable to residential sites;
A summary of procedures for obtaining approval from the ARC;
Attachments for such things as fences;
a definition section to define specific words
The Architectural Review Committee (ARC) consists of not more than three (3) persons who are appointed by the Board of Directors of the Homeowners Association from among the lot owners.
The address of the ARC will be the same as the address of the Managing Agent.

sections.title: Effect of Covenants and Resource Management Plan

blocks.x: The Declaration of Protective Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions (hereinafter “Covenants”) and the Resource Management Plan are documents governing property within Fossil Lake P.U.D. Particular areas or groups of lots become part of the Homeowners Association by annexation pursuant to a Supplemental Declaration. Copies of the Covenants, and of the Resource Management Plan, if applicable, are delivered to new home buyers when they purchase their homes and are available at any time at the ARC office and the HOA website. Each homeowner should review and become familiar with the Covenants and any Supplemental Declarations applicable to his or her property. Nothing in these Guidelines can supersede or alter the provisions or requirements of the Covenants, the Resource Management and Implementation Plan for Fossil Creek Reservoir Required Open Space - April 2003, or of any Supplemental Declaration and, if there is any conflict or inconsistency, the Covenants, the Resource Management Plan, and Supplemental Declaration will control. Provisions relating to the use of property and to improvements to property are found in Article IX of the Covenants.

sections.title: Effect of Governmental and Other Regulations

blocks.x: Use of property and improvements to property must comply with applicable building codes and other governmental requirements and regulations. Approval by the ARC will not constitute assurance that improvements comply with applicable governmental requirements or regulations or that a permit or approvals are not also required from applicable governmental bodies. Homeowners are responsible for obtaining all applicable permits or additional necessary approvals through the County or City. For general information about Larimer County and City of Fort Collins requirements, homeowners may write or call:
Larimer County Building Department, P.O. Box 1190, Fort Collins, Colorado 80522, 970-498-7700.
City of Fort Collins requirements, write or call the Fort Collins Building Department, P.O. Box 580, Fort Collins, CO 80522 970-221-6760.

In making improvements to property, homeowners are responsible for locating all water, sewer, gas, electrical, cable television or other utility lines or easements. Homeowners should not construct any improvements over such easements without the consent of the utility involved and homeowners will be responsible for any damage to any utility lines. The following list includes some of the contacts for locating underground utility lines and easements:
Utility Notification Center of Colorado (includes cable, gas and electric) 1-800-922-1987

Compliance with these Guidelines and Restrictions, the provisions of the Covenants, and the Resource Management Plan, if applicable, will help preserve the inherent architectural and aesthetic quality of Fossil Lake. It is important that the improvements to property be made in harmony with and not detrimental to adjacent property values or the community as a whole. A spirit of cooperation with the ARC and neighbors is paramount in creating an optimum environment that is mutually beneficial to all homeowners. When designing property improvements, it is important to consider potential impacts on adjacent property values as well as your own. By following these Guidelines and Restrictions and obtaining approvals for improvements to property from the ARC, homeowners protect their financial investment and insure that improvements to property comply with standards established for Fossil Lake Ranch. If a question ever arises as to the correct interpretation of any terms, phrases or language contained in these Guidelines and Restrictions, the ARC’s interpretation thereof shall be final and binding.

The intent of Fossil Lake Ranch P.U.D. Design Guidelines and Architectural Standards is to promote an increasingly open feel as one drives south and east through the development. Consequently, homes north of Lady Moon Drive have a five (5) foot minimum side yard setback, the minimum required by the City of Fort Collins. Homes south of Lady Moon down to the north section of Rookery have a seven-and-a-half (7.5) foot minimum side yard setback; homes south of Rookery and on Sagewater have a ten (10) foot side yard setback. Open Sale Estate lots nearer to the southern edge of the subdivision have fifteen (15) foot minimum side yard setbacks or are restricted to plated building envelopes. Additional standards related to fence types and required setbacks also enhance the increasingly open feel of the development, as does the specially mixed “Fossil Lake Green” required stain for all fencing.
The color is meant to unify the subdivision landscaping while blending these features into the background, further enhancing the signature FLR “open feeling.”

groups.label: Section II
groups.title: Specific Types of Residential Improvements – Design Guidelines

blocks.x: It is the responsibility of the homeowner to read, understand and comply with these design guidelines when making any proposed improvements. Following is a listing, in alphabetical order, of restrictions as well as a wide variety of specific types of improvements which homeowners typically consider installing, with pertinent information as to each.

UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFICALLY STATED (SEE SECTION 3.2), DRAWINGS OR PLANS FOR A PROPOSED IMPROVEMENT MUST BE SUBMITTED TO THE ARCHITECTURAL COMMITTEE AND THE WRITTEN APPROVAL OF THE ARCHITECTURAL COMMITTEE OBTAINED BEFORE THE IMPROVEMENTS ARE MADE.

In some cases, where it is specifically so noted, a homeowner may proceed with the improvement without advance approval by the Architectural Committee if the homeowner follows the stated guideline. In some cases, where specifically stated, a type of improvement is prohibited. If you have in mind an improvement listed below, Committee approval is required.
Approval not required: Replacement of existing tree or trees of the same type and location.
Committee approval is required. Approval will be based upon, but not limited to, the following criteria:
Must be of the same or generally recognized as complimentary architectural style and color as that of the residence.

Maximum sizes will be eight feet wide by ten feet long by eight-and-a-half feet in height (8’ x 10’ x 8 ½’) including skids, foundation or concrete slab. Requests for approval will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis, taking into consideration the lot size, square footage of the home and proposed location of shed or accessory building. Location must be shown in relation to the existing home and property lines
All sides must be “screened” from neighbors and the street view by a fence, vegetation, or the home.
Any utilities to accessory building shall be underground.
Location must be approved by the committee taking into consideration neighbors, fencing and street view and comply with all setback requirements for the lot.
The roof must match the existing roof on the residence.
Shall not unreasonably obstruct adjacent neighbor’s views of mountains, lakes or open areas.
Materials must match existing residence.
Premanufactured Accessory Buildings must be approved by the committee. The style and color must be complementary to the style and color of the home and follow the guidelines of 2.2b.

Note: A playhouse shall not be considered an accessory building if it is less than twenty-four (24 ) square feet and is less than six (6) feet in height from highest peak to ground. See Playhouses, Section 2.57.
ARC approval is required. Approval will be based upon, but not limited to the following criteria:

Additions or expansions to the home will require submission of detailed plans and specifications. Please refer to Section III of the design guidelines regarding submittal requirements. The plans shall include a site view layout showing the horizontal dimensions of the addition as well as setbacks. Elevation sketches shall be included that illustrate the architectural character of the addition/expansion as well as the height. A photo of the side of house where the addition will be located shall be included.
The addition/expansion materials and colors shall match the existing residence. All materials (siding, trim, roofing, stone, paint colors, etc.) shall be listed on the plans.
The location of the addition/expansion shall comply with the architectural height restrictions and setback requirements for the lot. Additions/expansions shall not be located over any easements.
ARC approval is required to relocate or replace existing numbers. Approval will be based upon, but not limited to the following criteria:
To allow for easy identification by visitors and emergency personnel, address numerals must be located on the front of the house in an easily visible location that is not obscured by landscaping.
Address numerals shall be a minimum of six (6) inches in height.
Address numerals shall be located at eye level and be near a porch light or illuminated at night.
The colors/materials for the address numerals shall contrast with the color of the house in order to be more visible.

All trade signs, which includes, but are not limited to landscaping, painting and roofing, may only be displayed while work is in progress and must be removed upon completion of the job. Sign may not exceed two by three feet (2’x3’). No signs shall be located on Association Common Fencing along common areas or greenbelts. Realty signs, see Signs, Section 2.68.

ARC approval is required for all air conditioning equipment including evaporative coolers (swamp coolers) and attic ventilators. No heating, air conditioning, air movement (e.g. swamp coolers) or refrigeration equipment shall be placed or installed on rooftops or extended from windows. Ground mounted or exterior wall air conditioning equipment located in the side yard must be installed in a manner so as to minimize visibility from the street and adjacent properties and to minimize noise to adjacent property owners. If necessary, screening may be required to reduce visibility. See also Evaporative Coolers, Section 2.26

Under Article IX, Section 15 of the Covenants, exterior radio antennae, television antennae, microwave or satellite dish antennae or other electronic signal, receiving or transmitting equipment may not be erected in residential portions of Fossil Lake unless approved by the ARC, or as otherwise allowed by State or Federal law. Due to the development of satellite antennae technology, the ARC, as a waiver and modification to the restrictions on antennae contained in Article IX, Section 15, adopts the following guidelines:

NOTE: ARC approval of a satellite dish is in no way to be construed as a representation, guaranty, warranty, etc., by the ARC and/or the Fossil Lake Homeowners Association that reception and/or transmission signals will be adequate or will remain undisturbed by vegetation or improvements located on surrounding properties Satellite dish/antennae must be in compliance with the following conditions:
Prior written approval of the ARC must be obtained, both before installation and before relocation of any previously approved existing satellite dish/antennae;

The satellite dish/antennae must be forty (40) inches or less in diameter and must be indistinguishable from other structures, devices or improvements otherwise allowed in the community and/or by the Covenants and/or these Guidelines;
Take neighbors views into consideration regarding placement of the satellite dish/antennae. The preferred location is not visible from the front street.

All cable/satellite dish lines running on the siding of the home shall be properly hidden for safety purposes and to not look in poor condition. Lines shall run parallel with the siding and trim boards.
All satellite antennae installed on a privately owned sites are restricted for the personal use of the owner of the site;
Antennae, radio antennae and other exterior radio or other antennae shall remain restricted from residential privately owned sites.
ARC approval is required. Refer to the following guidelines:

Canvas awnings are permitted. The awning shall be incorporated into the design of the patio. The color shall be the same as, or generally recognized as, a compatible color to the exterior of the residence.
The dimensions, product information and compatible canvas colors shall be submitted for review. A swatch or image of the canvas material to be used shall be provided.
See Decks, Section 2.21
ARC approval is required for every type of basketball goal. Refer to the following guidelines.
Permanent or sleeve-set pole mounted free-standing backboards may not be constructed in the “front” yard.
Garage mounted backboards may be approved.

Portable freestanding basketball boards may be conditionally approved if reasonably placed for play and properly stored when not in use. Properly stored shall mean that between Memorial Day and Labor Day annually, one portable basketball hoop may be stored within six (6) feet of a home if stored on the driveway of a lot, stands upright, and is in good repair. When in use, the goal must be positioned towards the inside of the lot (so that if a ball misses the goal, the ball goes into the owners property rather than into a neighbors lot or common area). Portable hoops must be located on a concrete surface.

At no time shall hoops be placed on the sidewalk, in the street, or within driveway curb cuts or the tree lawn area between the sidewalk and street. The Fossil Lake HOA will abide by the City of Fort Collins enforcement of basketball hoops or play equipment in the street under the Right of Way Encroachment Ordinance found in Chapter 23 Article 3 Obstructions & Encroachment, Section 23-46 Limitation, of the Municipal Code

“Rear” and “side” yard pole mounted basketball backboards and sport courts may be approved based upon, but not limited to, the following considerations: proximity of the goal to the property lines, proximity to the neighbor’s living area, size of court, landscaping and vehicles. Year-round landscape screening may be required.

Rear-yard sport courts for basketball backboards will be reviewed and approved on a case-by-case basis. The location of the court, size, materials, visibility and screening will all be considered during the review process. The use of sport courts may not cause excessive noise or disturbance to adjacent property owners.
Signs and basketball hoops in the public right of way can be considered a nuisance in the City of Fort Collins and will be dealt with by the City of Fort Collins.

ARC approval is not required if placed in “rear” yard and of a height not greater than three (3) feet including any pedestal. Placement in “front” or “side” yard requires ARC approval. Birdbath water shall be drained and replaced weekly to discourage pests such as mosquitoes.
Committee approval is not required for one “rear” yard installation. Size is limited to one-by-two feet (1' x 2'). Additional units or location in “front” or “side” yard requires ARC approval.
See Motor Vehicles/Recreational Vehicles, Section 2.48.
Each lot shall be used as a site for a residence and any business that operates from a residents to be reviewed for approval.
Approval must be obtained from the ARC for in-home business activity in which ANY of the following are true:
Clients will visit the property.
Inventory for sale or distribution will be stored at the property.
The business will cause traffic to increase in the neighborhood. Occasional deliveries by commercial package services will be excluded.
ALL of the following conditions must exist for approval to be granted:
The business complies with all requirements for home businesses specified by the City of Fort Collins.
The business is granted a license by the City of Fort Collins prior to submission for ARC approval.
Once granted, the City of Fort Collins license must remain active.
No more than two (2) client vehicles will be allowed to park in the neighborhood at any time regardless of the number of businesses licensed at the property.
Client vehicles must be parked in the homeowner’s driveway or garage and may not park in other parts of the neighborhood.
The business is not to result in a change from the normal residential restrictions including, but not limited to: trash, sound, order, signage, traffic, vehicles, parking and deliveries.
No sign advertising the business shall be displayed.
The request must be submitted to the ARC by the owner(s) of the property.
See Motor Vehicles/Recreational Vehicles, Section 2.48
Not permitted. See Sections 2.20 and 2.48 for allowable methods of vehicle storage.
See Driveways. See Section 2.25.
ARC approval is not required for temporary clothes lines or clothes drying structures in the backyard which can be, and are in fact, taken down after each use.
ARC approval is required. Refer to the following guidelines:

Compost bins or containers must not be immediately visible to adjacent properties. All bins or containers must be kept covered, well maintained and screened from adjacent properties and concealed from streets. Any wood structures used for composting must be painted to match the Fossil Lake Ranch fencing.
Composting shall not have any associated odors or associated pests.
Composting bins and/or methods shall be considered on a case-by-case basis.

A commercial vehicle is defined as, but is not limited to, a vehicle that has a business name or logo on it, has equipment attached to it, or is used for the purpose of providing services to an individual or corporation. An oversized vehicle is defined as a vehicle that cannot be parked within the garage. (See also 2.47 Motor Homes and 2.48 Motor Vehicles/Recreational Vehicles.) Refer to the following guidelines:

No lot shall be used as a parking or storage area for commercial or oversized vehicles except for a reasonable term while a structure on said lot is under construction. The managing agency must be notified, in writing, if said vehicle is to remain on the lot in excess of forty-eight (48) hours during any month. Written notification shall include an estimated date for removal of the vehicle.
All commercial vehicles must be parked in the garage.

Oversized vehicles or un-garage-able commercial vehicles must have ARC approval to be parked in the driveway. Approximate location and hours of parking must be included in the ARC approval request. Such approval will be based upon, but not limited to: no more than one vehicle, effect on curb appeal, effect on safety, and effect on street traffic.
No vehicle, whether commercial or oversized, shall be parked in such a manner that it blocks the sidewalk.
ARC approval is required. Refer to the following guidelines:

Decks, balconies and porches must be installed as an integral part of the residence and/or patio area. They must be located so as not to obstruct or diminish greatly the view of adjacent property owners or to create an “unreasonable” level of noise for adjacent property owners.

Construction shall not occur over any easements and the deck must be setback the required distance from property lines as defined by the setbacks for a given lot. (Refer to Section IV - Architectural Standards).
Decks, balconies and porches must be constructed from standard materials that coordinate with the house.
If they are painted, the color must match the body or trim color on the house. If the deck is stained, a compatible stain color must be utilized.
Elevated decks require masonry to be used on the columns or support posts. Covered decks and porches must use the same siding and roofing materials as the house.
ARC approval is required. Refer to the following guidelines:

Dog runs shall be located in the “rear” yard. They shall abut the home and be “screened” from adjacent property views. Dog runs are limited in size to two hundred and fifty (250) square feet and can be no higher than the existing perimeter fencing. Dog runs cannot run along adjoining property lines or extend beyond the back corners of the house into the side yard.
If a cover is used, the cover type and materials must be addressed in the request for approval. Tarpaulins are not allowed.
“Dog kennels” are not allowed.

Dog run fencing must match the type of fence (Type 1, 2, or 3) approved for the specific lot submitting the request. All fencing must be stained to match the Fossil Lake Ranch color. Refer to Appendix A for fencing types.
Invisible pet fencing is allowed. ARC approval is not required.

sections.title: Doors, Screen/Storm Doors and Garage Doors

blocks.x: ARC approval is not required for the addition or replacement of front doors, screen doors, garage doors or other type of doors to a home or an accessory building if the door style and color exactly matches the existing doors on the house. Security treatments for doors and windows must be approved by the ARC. All new door requests must comply with the following guidelines:

Storm doors and front doors - The style of the door shall be compatible with the architectural character of the house. The color of the door shall match the body or trim color of the house. Accent colors can be approved for storm and front doors if the proposed color is submitted for review with the current color scheme of the house.

Garage doors - The style of the door shall by compatible with the architectural character of the house. The color of new or repainted garage doors must match the body color of the house or blend with the body color range of the house. Brightly colored accent garage doors are typically not allowed.
ARC approval is required for any change affecting drainage. Refer to the following guidelines:

The design guidelines require that there be no interference with the established drainage pattern over any property. The established drainage pattern means the drainage pattern as engineered and constructed by the homebuilder prior (or in some cases, immediately following) conveyance of title from the homebuilder to the homeowner. The ARC may require a report from a drainage engineer as part of the landscaping or improvement plan approval process.

Adverse drainage affects to adjoining properties will not be tolerated. Article IX.8 of the Declaration of Protective Covenants requires that each lot owner be responsible for providing adequate water drainage from the lot into existing storm drains or street gutters so that water does not drain onto adjoining lots or open space.

Landscaping - Landscaping shall conform to the established drainage pattern. When installing landscaping, it is very important to insure that water drains away from the foundation of the house and that the flow patterns prevent water from flowing under or ponding near or against the house foundation, walkways, sidewalks and driveways. Water should flow over walkways, sidewalks or driveways into the street.
Fencing - When installing fencing, it is very important in insure that water drains away from the base of the fence and that flow patterns prevent water from ponding along the fence.

Berms - Berms shall be located a minimum of three (3) feet from all property lines and limited to three (3) feet in height above the nearest property line. When installing berms, it is very important that the established drainage pattern will not be disturbed. Upon completion of the berm, water must follow the original flow patterns and will not be permitted to flow onto adjoining properties/open space or cause ponding
Sump Pumps - Sump pump drainage shall be vented a reasonable distance from the property line, on the owner’s property, to allow for absorption.
Extension, expansion, or resurfacing of driveways requires ARC approval. See Motor Vehicles/Recreational Vehicles, Section 2.48. Refer to the following guidelines:
Any approved driveway expansion shall not be intended to promote the parking or storage of any vehicle off the driveway on a side yard.

To avoid long expanses of concrete driveways, the ARC requires the driveways to taper various widths at the curb/sidewalk. See Section IV Architectural Standards for width requirements for particular lots.

The ARC discourages the location of driveways being back to back on adjoining lots. The first property approved may determine whether the adjoining lots have right or left sided garages. In those cases where back-to-back driveways are unavoidable, additional setbacks from the side property line may be required along with enhanced landscaping to buffer the adjoining drives.

Minimum setbacks between driveways and property lines adjacent to the house is five (5) feet; minimum setbacks between driveways and property lines at streets vary throughout the development. See Section IV Architectural Standards for driveway setback requirements for particular lots.
See Air Conditioning Equipment, Section 2.6.
See Lights and Lighting, Section 2.45. Any additions or changes to the permanent original exterior fixtures (garage, front and rear doors) must be approved by the ARC.
(Refer to Appendix A for approved types, specifications and locations)

Association Common Fencing General Statement: Association Common Fencing is any fencing, whether installed by the Developer, builder or homeowner, that runs along or abuts open space, arterial streets, collector streets and local streets, and common walkways. Association Common Fencing may not be removed, replaced, painted a different color or altered, including adding a gate, without approval of the ARC. No signs shall be located on Association Common Fencing. If any Association Common Fences and/or walls which are located on a homeowner’s property are damaged or destroyed by the homeowner, the homeowner shall repair or recondition the fencing or wall at the homeowner’s expense.

Pre-approved Fence Design. All pre-approved fencing types, details and specifications are located in Appendix A, attached to these guidelines. Double fencing is not permitted. Fences planned to be located in the rear or side yards along property lines must be constructed exactly in accordance with the specifications found in Appendix A. It is recommended to obtain consent from adjoining lot owner.

Homeowner Installed Fencing and Gate Criteria: ARC approval for the location of homeowner installed fencing is required prior to installation by submitting a simple sketch, using the site plan of the lot showing the fence type, fence line, gates and any variations in height. The Fossil Lake Ranch Fencing Plan (Appendix A) outlines details on three approved fence types and are lot specific. Only approved fencing options will be considered. Gates installed in homeowner fencing must match the selected and approved fence style. Any applicable fencing permits from the City must be obtained prior to installation.

Fence sections which front or abut any public or private street, another front yard, common walkway, greenbelt/open space, park or non-urban area must be constructed such that the side of the fence which is generally accepted as being the more “finished” side faces said public or private street, common walkway, etc. The ARC will require a transitional section of fencing where it is applicable for symmetry and aesthetics. No electrical fences will be allowed. No plastic, chicken wire, hog wire, barbed wire or strand wire will be allowed.

Fence posts may be either cedar or pressure-treated wood. Wire mesh two by four inches (2”x4”) fabric, approved for Type 2 and Type 3 fence styles, may be applied only to the side of fence facing into homeowner lot. The wire fabric must be installed on the horizontal rail side of the fence, not stretched over posts. Extra care should be taken to avoid having any wire ends protruding. Newly installed fences must be stained within thirty (30) days of completion.

Drainage Under Fencing. Refer to Section 2.24 regarding drainage requirements. Certain drainage patterns may exist along or under proposed fence locations. It is very important to insure that water drains away from the base of the fence and that flow patterns prevent water from ponding along the fence. When constructing a fence, provide a space of two to three inches (2” to 3”) between the bottom of the fence and the ground elevation so as not to block these drainage patterns.

Gates: When installed in Association Common Fencing, gates must open INTO the homeowner’s lot rather than greenbelt/open space; cannot interfere with HOA sprinkler system or open space landscaping, and must be kept closed unless in use to exit/enter the property. Arbors and pergolas are not allowed on Association Common Fencing. All homeowner-installed gates will be of the approved design for the appropriate fence type.

Maintenance and Staining. Regular physical and aesthetic maintenance of fencing is required. The maintenance of the internal lot side of Association Common Fencing becomes the responsibility of each homeowner sharing that fence portion. The HOA will maintain the greenbelt or external side of Association Common Fencing. Stone columns will also be maintained by the Association. However, the homeowner is responsible for any damage done to Association Common Fencing and stone columns by the homeowner. (See Appendix A: Declaration of Fence and Landscaping Easement in Fossil Lake P.U.D, dated 10 January, 2000.)
Staining of all fences must be done with the approved stain for Fossil Lake Ranch. (Refer to Appendix A).

sections.title: Fire Pits, Chimineas, Outdoor Fireplaces and Firewood Storage

blocks.x: ARC approval is required for permanent outdoor fire pits and fireplaces. Portable outdoor fire pits and chimaeras do not require approval if located within reach of a working garden hose and in compliance with the following guidelines:
Any installation must comply with the requirements for the City of Fort Collins and the Poudre Fire Authority.

All permanent and portable outdoor burning devices must be located in the rear yard. Fire pits, chimineas and fireplaces must be incorporated into the overall design of the rear yard patio and/or deck area. The ARC may consider landscape screening to address any noise or visibility concerns.
Firewood must be located in the side or backyard, adjacent to the house; must be neatly stacked; and must not be located so as to block any existing drainage pattern on the lot.
ARC approval is required. Flagpoles may not exceed the height of the peak roof line of the house.
The HOA has pre-approved the American flag, and military service flags. College/university flags and sports team flags allowed on game day only. ARC approval is required for all other flags.

SPECIFIC GUIDELINES:
Turf Grass / Sod:

“Turf Grass” is defined by statute as “continuous plant coverage consisting of nonnative grasses or grasses that have not been hybridized for arid conditions, which, when regularly mowed, form a dense growth of leaf blades and roots.

You may choose to re-seed your lawn with less “thirsty” varieties of grass such as Buffalo Grass, Zoyia or Bermuda. You may also wish to consider using a non-vegetative turf grass or drought-tolerant vegetative landscape in the backyard. There is not one “perfect” turf grass for every situation, so you may wish to consult with a professional to determine which grasses are likely to do best with your soil and light conditions. You may choose any combination of turf grasses that work best for your site. Keep in mind that all grasses require regular watering when they are newly establishing themselves and will require some amount of watering thereafter to remain healthy. The goal is to minimize the total amount of water and fertilizer needed each year to maintain them.
Turf Grass Artificial Turf shall not be installed on slopes greater than six (6) percent.

General Appearance – Artificial turf shall be installed and maintained to effectively simulate the appearance of a well maintained lawn and shall have a minimum eight (8) year warranty against fading. The artificial turf must be a green color, similar to natural grass.

Maintenance – The following maintenance actives are required for artificial turf. Cleaning, sanitizing, brushing and removal of debris shall be required to maintain the turf in the best condition. The cleaning shall be done with a biodegradable product. There must be hand raking of worn turf areas on an as needed basis and the repair of depressions to maintain an even surface to prevent ponding of water.

The drawing or plan should be done to scale and should depict the property lines of your lot and the outside boundary lines of the home as located on the lot. All fencing shall be stained with the approved opaque stain, Fossil Lake Green. The approved stain color is on the file with Sherwin William’s Paint, refer to Appendix B - Definitions. Other companies such as Home Depot and Lowe’s may be able to color match a paint sample for use with their opaque deck/fencing stains. All wood surfaces shall be stained to meet the stain manufacturer's recommendations. The stain shall be reapplied as required to maintain uniform color and appearance. Power-washing the fence prior to re-application of stain is usually advised.

All gates installed in homeowner fencing must match the adjoining fence style. The gates shall be three (3) feet wide, measured from post to post and shall be centered within a fence section. Black metal hardware is required. No double gates are allowed, and all gates shall open into the homeowner's lot.

Where homeowner fencing abuts open space fencing, the height of both fences shall be identical. Homeowner fencing shall step down to meet the open space fencing. Each step-down shall be 6-inches in height lower than previous step and 8-feet long until the open space fencing height is met.

For Type 3 fencing, 2”x 4” woven wire fabric is allowed, but must be installed on the aide of fence facing into the lot. The wire fabric should be installed on the horizontal rails of the fence, not stretched over posts. Extra care should be taken to avoid having any wire ends protruding.

While cedar posts and railings are encouraged, pressure treated posts are now acceptable. All other construction design requirements remain the same. Please be advised that you may experience more twisting and splitting of non-cedar posts.

Adjacent: Properties that are not immediately next to each other but can be seen or viewed across property lines. (For example: properties that are from across a street or across greenbelts/open space.)
Adjoining: Properties that are immediately next to each other and share a common lot line.

Arbor: An arbor is a freestanding outdoor architectural structure that is smaller than a pergola constructed with vertical posts or pillars that support cross-beams and a sturdy open lattice. Arbors typically act as a garden accent or an element built over a walkway to pass beneath.
Awning: An Awning is a sheet of canvas or other fabric material stretched on a frame and used to keep the sun or rain off a patio, deck or window. Awnings can be operated mechanically or manually.
Boat: A boat is a structure designed for navigation on the water and propelled by oars, paddles, sails, or active power, and includes any object commonly understood to be a boat.
Camper Coach: An item of mounted equipment which, when temporarily or permanently mounted on a motor vehicle, adapts such vehicle for use as temporary living or sleeping accommodations.

Camping Trailer: A vehicular portable unit mounted on wheels and constructed with collapsible partial side walls which fold for towing by another vehicle and unfold at the campsite to provide temporary living quarters for recreational, camping or travel use.
Common Areas: Out lots that have been or will be dedicated to the Homeowners Association for the purpose of greenbelts, streetscapes, clubhouse, pool, waterfall, etc.
Complementary: Combining elements and colors in such a way as to enhance the qualities of each other.
Concealment: Requires that 80% of the area or object be hidden from the view of the adjacent properties.
Dog Kennel: A structure where animals are individualized for purposes of boarding, breeding or training or any type of commercial venture.
Dog Run: A contained space that is intended to allow one or more animals free movement in the out of doors.
Fossil Lake Ranch (FLR) Green Stain: Sherwin Williams’s product DB9602, Color FLS Green.
Gazebo: A gazebo is a freestanding roofed structure, typically octagonal, with open or latticework sides that offers a view of the surrounding area.

Greenhouse: A Greenhouse is a building or area usually made chiefly of glass, in which the temperature is maintained within a desired range to protect plants from cold weather. Greenhouses are typically used for cultivating tender plants or growing plants out of season.

Latticework: Latticework is an open framework made of strips of wood or similar material overlapped or overlaid in a regular, usually crisscross pattern. It is often seen as a component of arbors, pergolas, trellises, decks and gazebos. Latticework may also function as a privacy screen, often enhanced by having vines grown on it.
Legally Inoperable: A vehicle’s licensing status – e.g. expired plates.
Mechanically Inoperable: A vehicle’s physical status – e.g. car is not road-ready (motor dysfunctional, drive train out, flat tires, etc.)

Mobile Home: A mobile home is any type of trailer or vehicle body, regardless of any appurtenances, additions, or other modifications thereto, without independent active power, manufactured upon an integral chassis or under carriage and designed either for travel over the highways or for housing accommodations or both.
Motor Home: A vehicular unit, built on a self-propelled motor vehicle chassis, primarily designed to provide temporary living quarters for recreational, camping, or travel use.

Natural Resource Conservation Area: This is a 50-foot wide open space easement (south of Lots 17-20) which has been set aside from development and human access to provide a permanent buffer from human activity or contact with the wildlife of Fossil Creek Reservoir. No access is allowed.

Pergola: A pergola is an outdoor architectural structure that is similar to an arbor but much larger in scale. Pergolas may be attached to the back of the house or be freestanding and are constructed with vertical posts or pillars that support cross-beams and a sturdy open lattice. Pergolas tend to be located over patios or decks to provide shade.

Recreation Vehicle: A recreational vehicle is a vehicle-type unit primarily designed as temporary living quarters for recreational, camping, or travel use, which either has its own active power or is mounted on or drawn by another vehicle.

Raised Garden Bed: A garden bed that has been raised above the surface of the ground and framed by some type of hardscape materials such as timbers, brick, or decorative concrete block units. The average height of raised beds shall be between six (6) inches to eighteen (18) inches in height.
Screened: Requires that 50% of the area or object be hidden from the view of adjacent properties.
Sheen: Sheen is the degree of luster of a dried paint film. ARC will approve paint with an angular sheen of 0- 25 degrees for base and trim colors.
Trailer/Trailer House: A trailer is any vehicle coupled to, or drawn by any motor vehicle. A trailer house is a trailer designed to serve wherever parked as a dwelling or a place of business.
Travel Trailer: A vehicular portable unit, mounted on wheels, primarily designed and constructed to provide temporary living quarters for recreational, camping, or travel use.
Trellis: A trellis is similar to an arbor but smaller in size and more delicately featured. Trellises can be made from wood or wrought iron and can be purchased at a garden center.

Truck Camper: A portable unit, designed to be loaded onto, or affixed to, the bed or chassis of a truck, constructed to provide temporary living quarters for recreational, camping or travel use. This does not include pickup trucks ¾ ton or less in size with a topper or shell that does not exceed the height of the cab.

Xeriscaping Landscaping: Xeriscaping landscaping is a landscaping method developed especially for arid and semiarid climates that utilizes water-conserving techniques such as drought-tolerant plants, mulch, and efficient irrigation. Xeriscaping does not mean large expanses of exposed river rock or wood mulch without living plant coverage.
